key: And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying: ‘Deal gently for my sake with the young man, even with Absalom.’
s: Before the battle in which Joab kills Absalom, David charges his captains; Radak, on 18:5, reads it as a plea not to kill his son or strike him in anger, for though wronged by him, he is a father and has compassion.

evidence.gloss: [Radak, on 18:5, ‘Deal gently for my sake with the young man, even with Absalom’:] If you meet him in battle, deal gently with him for my sake and do not kill him, so that I may not look upon his harm; for though he did me evil, I am a father, to have compassion. And ‘gently’ means calmly, that is, do not come upon him in anger and rage to strike him, as would have been fitting; guard him for my sake.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok; ref 2 Samuel 18:5 and at [280,5] match). Read Radak on the whole of chapter 18 in the packet, with Rashi and Metzudat David on 18:5. Radak on 18:5 says: do not kill him, lest I see his harm; though he wronged me I am a father, to have compassion; and gently means do not come on him in anger and rage to strike him. The sentence’s reading (not to kill him or strike him in anger, for though wronged he is a father and has compassion) is carried by those words without drift. Plain sense fits 18:1 to 15 (Joab thrusts three darts through Absalom’s heart at 18:14). The killing is stated plainly. entry-check ok.
